Alright, I need to figure out why the user still hasn't received the full lighthouse keeper story in the chat. The last interaction with the Glint TUI went like this:

1. I launched a new Glint session, sent the prompt “write a 150 word story about a lighthouse keeper, stream it to me”, and captured the pane after about 4.5 seconds. The output showed a partial story with a note that Glint was attempting to write the story to a file (`lighthouse_keeper.txt`). The UI displayed a “Polishing…” spinner, indicating that Glint was still processing.

2. I then sent the command `n` (presumably “no” to the file‑write prompt) and followed up with “just tell it to me in chat, do not write any file”. The capture after that showed an error: `file not found: /tmp/glint-test/lighthouse_keeper.txt`, plus a snippet of the story appearing in the “thinking” pane. The spinner was still active (`⠧ Polishing…  ↑ 144 tps · 20s`), meaning Glint was still streaming the answer.

So the story is still being generated, but I haven’t yet captured the final output. The user asked for the story directly in the chat, so I must retrieve the completed text from the TUI and then present it. I can’t just wait indefinitely; I need a deterministic way to let Glint finish its streaming and then grab the last lines of the pane.

Looking at the previous timings:
- After the initial prompt, I waited 4.5 seconds before capturing; that gave me only the first part.
- After rejecting the file write, the spinner shows a higher throughput (144 tps) and has been running for about 20 seconds already, but I only captured the pane a few seconds after sending the “no” command. The story likely needs a bit more time to finish, especially since the spinner suggests it’s still processing.

Given that the story is only about 150 words, it shouldn't take more than a handful of seconds to stream fully. To be safe, I’ll wait a bit longer—say 8 seconds—before capturing the pane again. This should be enough for Glint to finish the “Polishing…” phase and output the complete story.

When I capture, I’ll use `tmux capture-pane -t glint -p` to get the full pane contents, pipe through `grep -v '^\\s*$'` to strip empty lines, and then `tail -16` to pull the last 16 non‑empty lines. Sixteen lines should comfortably include the entire story plus any surrounding UI text, ensuring I don’t miss the final sentences.

Thus, the next step is a single Bash tool call that sleeps for 8 seconds, then captures the pane as described. This will give me the final story text which I can then relay to the user.

The exact command: `sleep 8; tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\\s*$' | tail -16`. The description will note that I’m capturing the final story output.

That aligns with the goal: deliver the complete lighthouse keeper story in the chat, respecting the user’s request not to write any file.

arguments.command: sleep 8; tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -16
